questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Client: 'I am way out in the ocean.' Nurse: 'You seem to feel lonely.' This technique is:
questions.rationale: Translating into feelings verbalizes feelings expressed indirectly.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Communication Techniques (PDF p. 240)
questions.quote: You seem to feel lonely or deserted.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Client: 'I wish I were dead.' Nurse: 'Everybody gets down sometimes.' This response is:
questions.rationale: Equating intense feelings to 'everybody' belittles the client's distress.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Non-therapeutic Communication (PDF p. 240)
questions.quote: Everybody gets down in the dumps

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Why is challenging a delusion ('If you're dead, why is your heart beating?') nontherapeutic?
questions.rationale: Challenging causes the client to defend the delusion more strongly.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Non-therapeutic Communication (PDF p. 240)
questions.quote: Actually challenging causes the client to defend the

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Client: 'They look in my head with a TV camera.' Nurse: 'What channel?' This is:
questions.rationale: Literal responses treat figurative statements as fact; focus on feelings instead.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Non-therapeutic Communication (PDF p. 241)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: Client: 'I would like to die.' Nurse: 'Did you have visitors last night?' This is:
questions.rationale: Changing the subject takes the initiative away from the client and ignores suicide risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Non-therapeutic Communication (PDF p. 241)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: 'Everything will be all right' is which nontherapeutic technique?
questions.rationale: False reassurance devalues the client's feelings.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Non-therapeutic Communication (PDF p. 241)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: 'I'm sure your doctor has your best interest in mind' is an example of:
questions.rationale: Defending implies the client has no right to express opinions or feelings.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Non-therapeutic Communication (PDF p. 241)
questions.quote: I am sure your doctors has your best interest in mind.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client gives many details but eventually answers the question. This is:
questions.rationale: Circumstantial speech includes excessive detail but reaches the point; tangential never does.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thought Disturbances (PDF p. 242)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client repeats exactly what the nurse says. This is:
questions.rationale: Echolalia is repetition of another's words; echopraxia is imitation of movements.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thought Disturbances (PDF p. 242)
questions.quote: Client's imitation or repetition of what the nurse says.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client keeps returning to the same topic despite attempts to change it. This is:
questions.rationale: Perseveration is persistent adherence to one idea despite topic changes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thought Disturbances (PDF p. 242)
questions.quote: Persistent adherence to a single idea

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client says he is afraid of 'grittiz.' Invented words like this are:
questions.rationale: Neologisms are words invented by the client.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Thought Disturbances (PDF p. 242)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A client feels his body belongs to someone else. This is:
questions.rationale: Depersonalization is detachment or strangeness toward oneself; derealization is toward the environment.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Affect Disturbances (PDF p. 243)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: A catatonic client stays in an awkward position the nurse placed him in. This is:
questions.rationale: Waxy flexibility is maintaining positions for long periods even when awkward.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Motor Disturbances (PDF p. 243)
questions.quote: Maintaining the desires position for long periods of time

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: An older client fills memory gaps with made-up stories. This is:
questions.rationale: Confabulation fills memory gaps with fantasy believed by the teller, to maintain self-esteem.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Memory Disturbances (PDF p. 243)
questions.quote: Filling a memory gap with detailed fantasy believed by the teller

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: What is the major task of the PRE-orientation phase?
questions.rationale: Pre-orientation: self-awareness, data gathering, planning the first meeting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nurse-Patient Relationship (PDF p. 244)

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: Which phase is the longest and most productive?
questions.rationale: The working phase is longest; limit-setting and exploration occur here.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nurse-Patient Relationship (PDF p. 244)
questions.quote: Longest and most productive phase of the nurse-patient relationship

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: A client begins treating the nurse like his strict father. This is:
questions.rationale: Transference is the client unconsciously transferring feelings to the nurse; countertransference is the reverse.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Working Phase (PDF p. 244)
questions.quote: Client unconsciously transfers his feelings to the nurse.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.topic: Concepts of Mental Health & Therapeutic Models
questions.stem: The major task of the orientation phase is to:
questions.rationale: Orientation establishes rapport, trust, roles, and a mutually acceptable contract.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Nurse-Patient Relationship (PDF p. 244)
questions.quote: Major Task: develop a mutually acceptable contract
